A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same 3D-LATTE work, with matching authors, method, and experiments. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF contains an appendix or the separately referenced supplementary material; its contents cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 60 edits, CLIP and GPTEval3D results, qualitative component ablations, and a 57-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations on 100 edits, expanded baseline comparisons, attention visualizations, component ablations, and the retained user-study results.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the specified cross-attention selection rule: unmatched tokens or late denoising steps retain target attention. This changes the formal gate, while inversion, masking, geometry regularization, frequency annealing, and enhancement remain intact. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-guided appearance and geometry editing of assets from Objaverse and Google Scanned Objects. The increased asset and edit counts do not establish a new dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands from three baselines to six by adding Edit360, PDS, and InstructGS2GS. Edit360 also joins the qualitative comparison in Figure 5 and the GPTEval3D comparison in Table 2. The original three baselines remain, including in the unchanged user study.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the benchmark from 20 assets with three edits each, totaling 60 samples, to 25 assets totaling 100 samples. It also adds CLIP direction consistency to measure cross-view edit consistency. The existing CLIP metrics, GPTEval3D criteria, and 57-participant user-study design remain.

E4.justification: New Figures 3–4 examine token localization through cross-attention and semantic grouping through self-attention graph eigenvectors. The three component ablations in v1 Figure 6 are retained in v3 Figures 8–9 with revised displays. Newly mentioned supplementary quantitative ablations are not included in either supplied PDF.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The retained user-study percentages and additional benchmark scores do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 contain revised scores and substantial new result entries. For example, MVEdit's CLIP-dir/no-edit scores change from 0.11/0.080 to 0.121/0.077; v3 adds consistency scores and Edit360 GPTEval3D win rates of 67%, 90%, and 72%. These accompany an expanded benchmark and do not establish same-setting gains. User-study percentages remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The cross-attention definition changes from retaining target attention when CT(j) is None and t > tau_cross to retaining it when CT(j) is empty or t < tau_cross. This corrects the mathematical selection condition, including handling unmatched tokens. Other equation revisions mainly consolidate expressions or rename notation; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The introduction drops v1's explicit assertion of avoiding costly optimization procedures and explicitly contrasts the method with multi-view priors. The central training-free native-3D editing contribution and claims of superior editing quality remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new attention visualizations as evidence of token-to-Gaussian localization and semantic-part grouping. It also attributes Edit360's inconsistencies to fusion of original and edited view trajectories. Existing explanations of geometry regularization, frequency annealing, and enhancement largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-webpage address and specifies that mask-generation cross-attention is averaged over all time steps. These add access information and implementation clarification; the PDFs do not establish a code or data release.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Edit360, CMD, InstructGS2GS, InterGSEdit, and FreeInit, including a new discussion of Edit360's trajectory-alignment approach. The overall positioning against 2D-prior and hybrid editing methods remains. The duplicated Structured 3D Latents reference is not a new work.

P1.justification: The prose is locally shortened and clarified, attention notation is renamed, Methodology becomes Method, and numbered related-work subsections become unnumbered headings. The section sequence and most exposition remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, redesigns the teaser and pipeline diagrams, adds two attention-analysis figures, and transposes the baseline comparison while adding Edit360. Tables gain rows, a metric column, and ranking highlights. Existing ablations are split into separate figures with magnified details, while other displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 better supports the existing claims through broader baseline comparisons, a directly relevant cross-view consistency metric, and attention-mechanism visualizations. It also corrects the attention-selection equation. These are useful but bounded improvements within the same task and method: component ablations and user-study evidence largely remain unchanged, and the referenced supplementary analyses are unavailable in the supplied PDFs.
